review_notes: I reviewed all of Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Action/Rat.lean. It has four instances (DistribSMul and IsScalarTower for ℚ≥0 and ℚ) and no simp lemmas or attributes. The proofs use `rw [smul_def, ...]` and `simp only [smul_def, smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc]` locally, so nothing leaks into the global simp set. In Mathlib/Algebra/Field/Defs.lean, `NNRat.smul_def` and `Rat.smul_def` are plain theorems, not simp lemmas. I think that is deliberate. Making them simp would rewrite every `q • a` into `↑q * a` and could conflict with the smul-based simp normal form for module actions. I found no missing canonical simp lemma, wrong orientation, competing rules or cycle that the file's own contents support. I did not search downstream uses of these instances for simp-failure evidence. I can't run Lean, so I make no claim about simplifier behaviour.
